title: Minimum polynomial of an endomorphism under arbitrary scalar extension
statement: Let $K,L$ be fields [def-weil-field], let $\iota:K\to L$ be a unital field homomorphism, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and let $T:V\to V$ be $K$-linear. Let $W=L\otimes_K V$ be the $L$-vector space universal for $K$-bilinear maps out of $L\times V$, and let $T_L:W\to W$ be the $L$-linear map with $T_L(\lambda\otimes v)=\lambda\otimes T(v)$. Then $W$ is finite-dimensional over $L$. If $m_T\in K[X]$ and $m_{T_L}\in L[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] are the monic polynomials of least degree annihilating the two maps (equal to $1$ on the zero space), then $m_{T_L}=\iota_*m_T$, where $\iota_*$ applies $\iota$ to every coefficient. No perfectness or algebraicity hypothesis on $K$ or $L/K$ is required.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168: supporting minimum-polynomial scalar-extension lemma for the matrix argument. This exact equality is supplied by the agent, not asserted as a named theorem in Milne; the report gives its coefficient-matrix proof.

proof.text: If $\iota(a)=0$ and $a\ne0$, then $1=\iota(a^{-1})\iota(a)=0$, impossible. Thus identify $K$ with $\iota(K)\subset L$. Choose a finite spanning list of $V$ and repeatedly delete a vector expressible through the others. A dependence expresses a vector through the others by dividing by a nonzero coefficient. Each deletion preserves the span; the resulting finite list $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ is independent and spans, hence is a basis.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168; agent-supplied coefficient-matrix argument supporting scalar extension, not a named theorem of Milne.

proof.text: By [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], $e_j\otimes1$ is a basis of $V\otimes_KL$. The mutually inverse maps $v\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes v$ and $\lambda\otimes v\mapsto v\otimes\lambda$ are well-defined by the balancing relations, so $1\otimes e_j$ is a basis of $W$. In particular $W$ is finite-dimensional. If $n=0$, both spaces are zero and both minimum polynomials are $1$, proving the assertion. Assume $n>0$.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168; agent-supplied coefficient-matrix argument supporting scalar extension, not a named theorem of Milne.

proof.text: Write $T(e_j)=\sum_i a_{ij}e_i$ and $A=(a_{ij})$. Then $T_L(1\otimes e_j)=\sum_i\iota(a_{ij})(1\otimes e_i)$, so its matrix is $A_L=(\iota(a_{ij}))$. Composition of maps has matrix product because its $(i,j)$ entry is $\sum_k a_{ik}b_{kj}$; The zeroth powers have identity matrices, and multiplying once more by $A$ or $A_L$ gives by induction matrices $A^r$ and $A_L^r=\iota_*(A^r)$ for all powers. Hence for every $p\in K[X]$, the matrix of $(\iota_*p)(T_L)$ is $\iota_*(p(A))$. Put $d=\deg m_T$ and $q=\iota_*m_T$. The polynomial $q$ is monic of degree $d$ and annihilates $T_L$, since $m_T(T)=0$.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168; agent-supplied coefficient-matrix argument supporting scalar extension, not a named theorem of Milne.

proof.text: The arrays $I,A,\ldots,A^{d-1}$ are $K$-linearly independent: a nonzero relation gives a nonzero polynomial $p$ of degree $r<d$ with $p(T)=0$, and dividing $p$ by its nonzero leading coefficient gives a monic annihilating polynomial of degree $r$, contradicting the defining minimality of $m_T$. Also $d>0$, since the only monic constant polynomial is $1$ and its value is the nonzero identity of $V$.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168; agent-supplied coefficient-matrix argument supporting scalar extension, not a named theorem of Milne.

proof.text: Regard these arrays as vectors in $K^{n^2}$, indexed by pairs $(i,j)$. By [lem-weil-linear-independence-field-extension] their coefficientwise images $I,A_L,\ldots,A_L^{d-1}$ remain $L$-linearly independent. Thus no nonzero polynomial over $L$ of degree less than $d$ annihilates $T_L$. Since $q$ is monic of degree $d$ and annihilates $T_L$, the least degree of a monic annihilator is exactly $d$, so $\deg m_{T_L}=d$.

source.place: Section 9b, printed pp.166,168; agent-supplied coefficient-matrix argument supporting scalar extension, not a named theorem of Milne.

proof.text: The leading terms of the monic polynomials $m_{T_L}$ and $q$ cancel, so their difference is either zero or has degree less than $d$. Its value at $T_L$ is zero. The independence just proved excludes a nonzero such difference, whence $m_{T_L}=q=\iota_*m_T$. None of these steps used perfectness, algebraicity, separability, or finiteness of $L/K$.
